# Other languages

Any language works when it builds a **WASI preview 1 program**: a module with a `_start` function that imports nothing but `wasi_snapshot_preview1`, and uses only WebAssembly 2.0 (no GC, no exception handling, no threads). Load it and `$wasm.modules()` says at once whether it runs: a module that needs anything else shows an error that says what.

The languages below weren't tried for these docs. What's said of each is what its own tools document.

| Language | Fits? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Swift | Yes | The Swift SDK for WASI (`swift build --swift-sdk wasm32-unknown-wasi`) builds WASI preview 1 programs. Foundation makes modules several MB, so a first call compiles for a long time and every call holds more memory. |
| C# / .NET | Likely too big | .NET's WASI build carries its runtime: tens of MB, over the default `MaxModulesMB`. |
| Nim, Odin, D | Through C or LLVM | Each can target `wasm32-wasi`, through C (`zig cc`) or its own LLVM backend. |
| Grain, MoonBit | Check the target | Both build WebAssembly; a module runs here only if their WASI output is preview 1 with no other imports. |
| Kotlin/Wasm, Dart, Java (WasmGC) | No | They need WebAssembly GC. |
| Python, Ruby, JavaScript | Not as interpreters | An interpreter built for WASI (CPython, Ruby, QuickJS) needs its standard library as files, and no folder is mounted. A tool that bundles the script and interpreter into one preview 1 program (Javy's static mode for JavaScript) can work, at a few MB per module. For JS, your page code is already JavaScript. |

To check a module without an app, run it with the [wazero CLI](https://wazero.io), which runs it with the same engine:

```bash
wazero run mymodule.wasm --describe
echo '{"text":"hi"}' | wazero run mymodule.wasm run
```

Then copy it to `pb_hooks/<name>.pb.wasm` and look at `$wasm.modules()`: a module that can't run says why there.
